title: simo seed
description: A seed describes a simulated world: device classes with hidden state machines, what they log, how many devices exist, what goes wrong and who fixes it. Seeds are YAML; this schema describes the YAML structure. Run validate_seed for checks this schema cannot express (references between states, events, patterns and vocabularies, and lint warnings).

master_seed.description: Master random seed. The same seed and spec always give the same data.

patterns.description: Named rate multipliers over time, referenced from event rates, e.g. rate: 0.03/s * store_hours.

vocab.description: Named word lists for {name:vocab} slots in message templates.

fleet.description: How many devices of each class exist.

faults.description: Scheduled faults. Each gets a ground-truth cause id that labels the events it causes.

state_name.description: A state of the same class. Hyphens are allowed, e.g. SYN-SENT.

duration.description: A duration: 90s, 10m, 1.5h, 7d, or a bare unit like day.

rate.description: Events per unit of time: 0.03/s, 1/2h (once per two hours), 0.5/day.

distribution.description: A number or a distribution: uniform(a, b), normal(mean, sd), lognormal(mu, sigma), exp(mean). Durations are allowed as arguments where a time is meant, e.g. exp(30m).

tick.description: Simulation step, at least 1ms. 1s suits most worlds; use 100ms for fast protocols.

fourier.description: F(t) = 1 + sum of amp * cos(2 pi k (t - peak) / period), clamped at 0. Pattern time starts on Monday 00:00 UTC, so a 7d period starts on Monday.

items.description: [k, amplitude, peak]: harmonic number, amplitude (0.9 = strong), and the time within the period when it peaks, e.g. [1, 0.9, 14h].

zipf.description: Zipf exponent: 0 is uniform, about 1 means a few words dominate.

class.description: A device class: a hidden state machine plus what it emits.

initial.description: Initial state; default is the first state listed.

states.description: States in order. Each lists where it can go and by which law.

commands.description: Actions operators can take, e.g. restart.

health.description: A hidden value in [0, 1], starting at 1, that drifts and drives health_rate transitions: falling health raises failure rates before anything breaks.

drift.description: Change per time, usually negative, e.g. -0.03/day.

noise.description: Standard deviation per square root of a day.

emit.description: Event ids emitted on entering this state.

transition.description: A rate like 1/2h (memoryless), health_rate(0.5/day, gamma: 6) (rate x exp(gamma x (1 - health))), fixed(90s) (after a fixed time in the state) or on_command(restart) (only when that command runs).

theta.description: How fast it returns to the mean, e.g. 1/10m.

in_state.description: State -> change while in that state.

event.description: A log line template and when it fires.

text.description: Message with up to 5 placeholders {name:generator(args)|format}. Generators: hex(n), int(a, b), uniform(a, b), normal(mean, sd), lognormal(mu, sigma), exp(mean), choice(a, b, ...), vocab or vocab(name), ip(cidr), uuid, metric(name) (the device's current value), seq (per-device counter). Formats: %d, %.2f, %x. Write {{ for a literal brace.

rate.description: Base rate times patterns, e.g. 0.03/s * store_hours. Omit for events only emitted on entering a state or by a command.

tags.description: Labels that fault effects can target.

only_in.description: States in which the event can fire; all others count as x0.

excite.description: Hawkes self-excitation (bursts). Planned for phase 4; accepted but ignored.

reset_health.description: Set health back to 1, e.g. a restart clears a leak.

fleet_entry.description: Expands one class into devices: either count, or sites with per_site.

name.description: Device name pattern with {site}, {n} (index in site), {i} (index in entry), {class}; widths like {site:02}.

jitter.description: Per-device variation: rate_scale (multiplies all event rates) or <metric>.mean (added to a metric's mean).

at.description: Start: "day2 09:15" (day 1 is the first) or an offset like 26h.

for.description: Length; omit to last until the end.

target.description: Devices: site[7]/pos_terminal[*], pos_terminal[3] or site[*]/pos_terminal[1]. Indexes are 1-based.

label.description: Human description for the answer key.

effect.description: Exactly one of multiply or health.

tag.description: Event tag to multiply, or * for all events of the class.

health.description: Added to health when the fault starts, e.g. -0.3.

responder.description: Notices devices entering any of states and, after the delay, runs command if it is allowed in the device's state at that moment (so it still fixes a crash-looping device that is briefly running).
